title: Hidden Inflammation in Hyperpigmented Lesions: Molecular Assessment of Epidermal Activity and Implications for Disease Scoring in Patients with Skin of Color
summary:
Atopic dermatitis (eczema) is an inflammatory skin disease. Clinicians often assess disease activity based on visible skin changes, for example by evaluating skin redness (erythema).

In individuals with more strongly pigmented skin, however, erythema may be more difficult to detect. Inflamed skin areas may instead appear darker, grayish, or violaceous. As a result, the degree of inflammation may be underestimated.

It is currently not well understood whether such darker-appearing skin lesions still contain active inflammation in the superficial layers of the skin. If this is the case, disease activity may be underestimated in some patients.

This study aims to improve our understanding of whether such lesions remain inflammatory. The findings may contribute to improved assessment of disease activity across different skin types in the future.

We will investigate whether skin areas that appear darker and show little or no visible erythema are nevertheless inflamed. To do this, superficial skin samples will be collected using a gentle adhesive tape method (tape stripping) and analyzed in the laboratory for inflammatory markers. Specifically, we will assess whether typical inflammatory markers that are commonly elevated in atopic dermatitis are present in these samples and to what extent. These markers will be analyzed at the protein level as well as at the molecular level (RNA). In addition, we will compare inflammatory marker profiles between different types of skin lesions (e.g., darker-appearing versus erythematous lesions).

The results may help to determine whether disease activity is underestimated in individuals with more strongly pigmented skin.

Patients with atopic dermatitis
Adult patients (≥18 years) with a clinically confirmed diagnosis of atopic dermatitis and at least one suitable skin lesion are assessed during a single study visit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants may include patients of all Fitzpatrick phototypes (I–VI). The Fitzpatrick phototype will be assessed and documented at the time of study inclusion.

For the purpose of describing the study population, lighter phototypes are defined as Fitzpatrick I–III and darker phototypes as Fitzpatrick IV–VI. The latter are commonly referred to in the dermatological literature as “skin of color.”

An approximately balanced distribution of phototypes, particularly between these groups, will be aimed for in order to enable exploratory comparative analyses. This classification is used exclusively for analytical purposes and does not constitute an inclusion criterion.

Inclusion criteria:
• Age ≥ 18 years
• Clinically confirmed diagnosis of atopic dermatitis
• Presence of at least one lesion suitable for tape stripping
• Capacity to provide informed consent and written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute skin infection in the intended sampling area
• Severe excoriations or ulcerations at the sampling site
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
